subject: Private VPC control-plane: rollback, mitigation, and postmortem
messages:
From: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.ramirez@acme-ops.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: dl-infra@acme-ops.com
Date: 2026-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Control plane connectivity failure in our VPC — immediate help needed

Laura,

We began seeing 503s for control-plane calls from our private deployment this morning at ~08:40 PT. The inference nodes continue to run, but attempts to reach the Redwood control plane (for model routing and rollout state) are failing with TLS handshake errors and connection resets. This is impacting automated rollouts and some management APIs (cannot pin versions, cannot rollout canaries).

We've already placed a manual emergency hold on auto-rollouts but customers are noticing degraded behavior in our app. Can your team confirm scope and advise mitigation steps (rollback, temporary bypass, etc.)? We have logs attached to this email.

— Jorge
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
(attachment: acme_controlplane_client_logs_030226.log)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.ramirez@acme-ops.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: [ACTION] Acme: VPC control-plane connectivity — triage + mitigation

Team,

Acme reporting TLS handshake failures to the private control plane in their VPC (reported 08:40 PT). They are seeing 503s and management operations failing. Impact: unable to change rollout state; inference continues but we risk drift and customer-visible anomalies.

Immediate asks:
- Rohan: collect redwood-control-plane agent logs from the 03/02 08:30–09:30 PT window and X509 cert chain material from the customer-facing endpoint.
- Markus: validate whether yesterday's control-plane agent deployment (canary -> prod) included a change to TLS/ALPN or cert validation logic.
- Hannah: reach out to Acme (Jorge) with a short mitigation note — avoid alarm, provide rollback ETA.
- Neha: prepare an internal rollback plan; include steps for customers on how to temporarily switch to local-only inference (if needed) and a runbook for re-syncing state after rollback.

I'll coordinate with Jorge and provide status updates.

— Laura
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Acme: VPC control-plane connectivity — triage + mitigation

Laura / team,

I pulled the agent logs from the timeframe Jorge pointed to — attaching a zip with the controlplane_agent and openssl traces. Early sign: intermittent "tlsv1 alert protocol version" and "unexpected message" entries from the agent side. Correlation shows the agents that upgraded yesterday (2026-03-01 22:00 UTC rollout) are showing the failures.

Hypothesis: a small TLS stack change in the new agent (TLS client hello extension ordering) is causing handshake rejections by certain customer-side VPC gateways that enforce strict cert/ALPN semantics. This would explain why inference processes stay up but management calls fail.

Next steps:
- I'm preparing a rollback of the agent to the prior build and will validate handshakes against Acme's gateway in a staging slice.
- Markus, can you confirm which commit introduced the TLS change?

— Rohan
(attachment: controlplane_agent_logs_20260302.zip)

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Acme: VPC control-plane connectivity — triage + mitigation

Rohan — confirmed. The 2026-03-01 rollout included a minor dependency bump in our TLS client library and a guard that reorders ALPN entries for perceived compatibility with some cloud NATs. Commit id: 5e8b3c4 — change in client_hello ordering.

I'll prepare an immediate hotfix branch (revert behaviour to previous ordering) and a fast rollback pipeline. We should coordinate rollback windows with Acme operations.

— Markus
VP, Platform Engineering

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.ramirez@acme-ops.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Update: Mitigation plan and rollback ETA for your VPC control-plane issue

Hi Jorge —

Thanks again for the quick report and the logs — very helpful. Short, plain update from our side:

What we found (high level):
- We identified a recent control-plane agent change (rolled 2026-03-01) that alters TLS client hello ordering. Some VPC gateway appliances validate ALPN/cipher ordering strictly and reject the handshake, which explains the TLS errors you sent us.

Immediate mitigation we're executing now:
1) We will perform a rollback of the control-plane agent to the prior build in a staged fashion.
2) We will coordinate a rolling restart of the agent in your VPC between 14:00–14:30 PT to minimize disruption. During that window, management operations (pinning, rollouts) may be briefly unavailable; inference traffic should remain serving.
3) Post-rollback we will validate control-plane connectivity and re-sync rollout state.

ETA: rollback window scheduled for 2026-03-02 14:00 PT. We will share a live status update and an aggregate postmortem within 72 hours.

If you prefer we can apply a customer-side NAT/ALPN rule as a stop-gap, but we recommend the rollback for a permanent fix.

I'll be on the call during the rollback; reach me directly at +1 (415) 555-0192 if anything becomes urgent.

— Laura
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.ramirez@acme-ops.com>, dl-infra@acme-ops.com
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Postmortem & closure: private VPC control-plane connectivity for Acme Corp

Jorge / Acme infra team —

Postmortem summary (attached: redwood_postmortem_acme_20260305.pdf; supporting logs attached):

Incident timeline — highlights:
- 2026-03-01 22:00 UTC: control-plane agent rollout (includes TLS client_hello ordering change, commit 5e8b3c4).
- 2026-03-02 08:40 PT: Acme reported TLS handshake failures and 503s for management APIs.
- 2026-03-02 09:35 PT: Redwood triage confirmed correlation with the new agent build.
- 2026-03-02 14:00 PT: Staged rollback performed for Acme's VPC; handshakes validated and connectivity restored by 14:18 PT.

Root cause:
A change in TLS client_hello ALPN/cipher ordering in the new control-plane agent triggered handshake rejections by certain strict VPC gateway implementations. The change was introduced as a compatibility tweak but had insufficient cross-environment validation in pre-release tests.

Customer impact:
- Management/control-plane API failures for ~5–6 hours in the observed window until rollback; inference serving remained operating but some automated rollout activity was paused.

Remediation & long-term actions:
1) Immediate: rollback for affected customers and production validation (completed 2026-03-02).
2) Hotfix: we reverted the TLS ordering change in the agent, published 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC.
3) Testing: expanded our pre-release matrix to include strict ALPN/cipher validation against representative gateway appliances (wired + cloud NATs).
4) Canarying: add a short canary phase for control-plane agent TLS changes that exercises customer-like gateway validations before broad rollout.
5) Runbooks: published a Private VPC control-plane rollback runbook and automated rollback playbook in our ops repo.
6) Customer compensation: we are issuing a partial service credit for the affected window; Hannah will coordinate details with your procurement team.

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_acme_20260305.pdf, controlplane_agent_logs_20260302.zip

If you have questions or want a walkthrough of the postmortem, we're happy to set up a short call. Thanks for your patience and for working with us to get this resolved.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
